Frontier AI coding just became free to deploy. Two models. One week. Everything changed.

Moonshot AI open-sourced Kimi K2.7 Code — a trillion-parameter model built specifically for agentic coding that outperforms its predecessor while consuming fewer resources. Days later, Poolside released Laguna M.1 under Apache 2.0: 225B parameters, 256K context window, and designed to run on hardware your team already has.

This is the moment the economics of AI-powered development permanently shifted. Until now, frontier-class code generation required expensive API subscriptions to proprietary platforms. These releases break that dependency.

Enterprise teams can now self-host models that compete with the best commercial offerings — with full control over fine-tuning, data privacy, and cost. No per-token fees. No vendor lock-in. No waiting for someone else's roadmap.

But access alone is not advantage. The organizations that move fastest to integrate, customize, and scale these models into real workflows will define the next phase of software development.
